pue.boundary: Colossus and Colossus II or SpaceX AI fleet
pue.basis: SpaceX explicitly defines nameplate compute draw as installed GPUs times their respective all-in GPU power draw, excluding cooling, distribution losses, lighting, security and facility overhead; it is an IT-load exit metric, not facility energy, actual consumption or utilization. Site grid and turbine capacities do not provide matching-period facility and IT energy, so no defensible PUE can be inferred.
pue.aggregation_rule: sum(facility_energy)/sum(IT_energy), equivalently IT-energy-weighted site PUE; unavailable

model.revenue_scope: Recognized incremental AI infrastructure revenue from the initial ramp of new cloud service agreements; exclude advertising and do not substitute broader subscriptions, data licensing or API revenue
model.capacity_time_basis: 91-day Q2. Bound period-average total nameplate IT draw between 1.0GW Q1 exit and 1.4GW Q2 exit; use 1.2GW linear-ramp base. Exact activation dates, external allocation and utilization are undisclosed.

formulas.average_nameplate_interval_bound: Q1 exit <= Q2 average total nameplate IT draw <= Q2 exit; base=(Q1 exit+Q2 exit)/2
formulas.recognized_cloud_per_total_nameplate_mw_: Q2 recognized incremental cloud revenue * 4 / average total nameplate IT MW / 1e6
formulas.canonical_rate: Q2 recognized external cloud revenue * 4 / average external effective utilized IT MW / 1e6
formulas.pue_sensitivity: If matching average facility MW F and PUE are reported, IT_MW=F/PUE; effective_IT_MW=F/PUE*physical_utilization
formulas.jevons: d/(1-d), only with scoped realized price decline and matched paid task or token volume; currently unidentifiable

assumptions.input: Q2 average total nameplate IT draw
assumptions.basis: Linear-ramp base between filed/issuer Q1 and Q2 exits; 1.0GW and 1.4GW are hard bounds absent retirements. Results are shown as 1.0-1.4GW range rather than presenting 1.2GW as reported.
No measured utilization or capacity allocation was disclosed; therefore the canonical effective-MW output is blank.
No measured site/fleet facility energy and IT energy or quantitative design target was disclosed. No universal proxy is imported.

rejected_shortcuts: No Q2 revenue divided by the 1.4GW quarter-end metric without a period-average reconstruction.
No assumption that all Colossus nameplate capacity was allocated to paying cloud customers rather than internal Grok or other workloads.
No nameplate draw treated as actual consumption or utilization; the filing expressly rejects that interpretation.
No turbine/grid generation capacity ratio treated as PUE.
No total AI segment or group ARR divided by AI MW.
No contracted sales, backlog or fixed monthly fee treated as recognized Q2 revenue.
No management payback claim treated as audited cohort cash return.
No exact Jevons break-even without matched realized token/task price and volume.

structured_deals.economic_effect: Q2 initial ramp generated $1.6B incremental AI infrastructure revenue. Fixed monthly fees are recognized with phased capacity availability then straight-line at steady state. Agreements generally become terminable by either party on 90 days' notice after an initial ramp period, and one unnamed AI customer represented 19.5% of consolidated Q2 revenue. Contracted Q3 sales of $6.7B cover six months starting to ramp in October, but are not Q2 revenue or durable RPO.

Approximately 110,000 NVIDIA GPUs plus related components for $920M per month at full fee from October 2026 through June 2029, subject to delivery and termination terms. The $100,364 per stated GPU-year dimensional rate is not MW-normalized and includes CPU, memory and related components.

Colossus 1 capacity for training, fine-tuning, inference and HPC; monthly fee runs through May 2029 with a reduced May 2026 ramp fee, but either party may terminate on 90 days' notice. The filing does not disclose capacity, fee or utilization.

$13.329B current plus long-term debt at June 30 and $327M Q2 interest expense. The April 24 Valor III five-year equipment lease alone carried $6.587B undiscounted payments. Asset ownership/form accounting does not remove fixed financing exposure or replacement risk.
$25B across five tranches due 2031-2056, weighted coupon 5.855%, partially used to repay a $20B bridge. This lengthens funding but is corporate, not project-matched AI nonrecourse financing.

$27.955B at June 30, primarily AI infrastructure, third-party cloud capacity, other services and the Spectrum Transaction; $22.244B falls due in 2027. Different perimeters prevent adding this mechanically to Valor debt or AI capex.
Approximately $2B for mobile gas turbines and related packages to power data centers. Generation capacity and permit status do not establish IT load, facility energy or PUE.

findings: Strongest finding: the first recognized-revenue/nameplate diagnostic is $4.57-$6.40M per total nameplate IT MW-year (base $5.33M), using $1.6B Q2 new-cloud revenue and a 1.0-1.4GW average-nameplate bound. It is not the canonical effective-utilized-MW rate because capacity includes internal use and utilization is missing.

The filed Q2 nameplate definition resolves the power boundary as an IT-load exit metric while expressly excluding facility overhead and actual utilization. This invalidates the old 100% utilization/PUE=1 placeholders.

The primary earnings transcript confirms management's separate $30-$50 per watt monetization best guess, but its Rubin/future perimeter and unresolved time/power boundary make it guidance, not a realized Q2 comparison.

Management's less-than-one-year payback claim cannot be reconstructed from the $15.828B Q2 AI capex because capex, activation, customer allocation, cash margin and contracted versus recognized revenue are not cohort matched.

Capital exposure is material: $13.329B related-party Valor failed-sale-leaseback debt, $27.955B consolidated noncancelable commitments and $25B corporate bonds. These amounts have different perimeters and are not summed.
Customer concentration/tenor matters: one unnamed AI customer was 19.5% of Q2 consolidated revenue, while cloud agreements generally become terminable on 90 days' notice after ramp.
gaps: Dated Q2 activations/retirements and external-versus-internal allocation of the 1.0-1.4GW nameplate fleet.
Measured physical utilization, facility energy, IT energy and site-level IT-energy weights; no reported or defensible modeled PUE.
Cloud-only recognized revenue by customer and full customer exhibits, including prepayments, customer-supplied hardware, service credits, guarantees and delivery schedules.
Cohort-matched capex, cash margin, financing, PPA/fuel cost and replacement schedule needed to test the less-than-one-year payback claim.
Counterparty identity for Customer B and reconciliation to Google, Anthropic and other cloud agreements without inference.
Matched realized token/task pricing, paid volume and energy per task required for Jevons and open/proprietary economics.
